paper_id: Revisit Self-Debugging with Self-Generated Tests for Code Generation
title: Revisit Self-Debugging with Self-Generated Tests for Code Generation
motivation: Oracle tests unavailable in real-world scenarios; self-generated tests for self-debugging lack full exploration of limitations
problem_framing: Evaluate self-debugging with self-generated tests across basic (HumanEval/MBPP) and competitive (LiveCodeBench) programming tasks
key_insight: Bias from self-generated tests causes false negatives; in-execution (intermediate states) avoids this bias vs post-execution (output comparison)
method_signature: Two paradigms: post-execution (compare outputs) vs in-execution (analyze runtime traces per basic block)
evaluation_criteria: Pass rate on benchmark tests (HumanEval+, MBPP+, LiveCodeBench); test suite accuracy measurement
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Post-execution self-debugging with self-generated tests causes performance declines on basic problems; models struggle to recognize faulty feedback
evidence_for_taste: post-execution self-debugging struggles on basic problems
performance on MBPP may improve initially but ultimately become worse
The model is expected to determine whether failure is due to bugs in program or errors in the test
efficacy depends not only on model ability to identify defects but also on ability to recognize faulty feedback
thinking_moves: 对比post-execution与in-execution两种反馈模式的适用边界
从性能不一致反推bias引入机制
区分test质量与program正确性的判断能力
通过program contracts量化self-generated test的有效性
cites_own_work: Kechi Zhang et al., Self-edit: Fault-aware code editor for code generation, ACL 2023
Li Zhong et al., Debug like a human, ACL 2024
